comments.text: The character set of the first scene, the walk back to the village: 2 KB to $5FFF, multicolour, shown at $D018 = $16 (screen $4400, characters $5800 in VIC bank 1). The scene's screen (village_screen) uses 142 of its characters.

Character $4F of village_chars. The label is the engine's: in the attract block, wipe_char_set redefines character $4F of the title's character set, which sits at these addresses then; the ending does not touch it.
village_chars from character $57.
village_chars from character $80 to the end of the set at $5FFF.
The ending's sprite shapes, 44 blocks of 64 bytes to $6AFF (pointers $80-$AB in VIC bank 1). This first one, a filled disc, is never shown: no animation starts below $81.

Sprite $81, the first frame of the sparkle a heart turns into (animation 15): rays round an empty middle, a single-colour shape. The label is the engine's: in a level, weapon_icon_draw writes the panel's weapon icon here.
Sprite $82, the sparkle's second, wider frame. The label is the engine's, as at $6040.
Sprite $83, empty: the sparkle's last frame, so a heart that has burst disappears.
Part of the empty sprite $83. The label is the engine's (weapon_icon_draw's second half in a level).
Sprites $84-$88: a fuzzy walking left, multicolour (light red with dark grey and yellow). Animation 0 swings back and forth through them.
Row 13 of sprite $84. The label is the engine's (weapon_icon_draw, in a level).
Sprites $85-$88, the rest of the walk to the left.
Sprites $89-$8D: the same fuzzy walking right (animation 1). Clyde and the plain members of the posse use these.
Sprite $8E: the plain fuzzy facing out of the screen. Animation 2 shows it, and no scene starts animation 2.
Sprites $8F-$93: the fuzzy with a bow on its head turning from left, through facing out ($90-$92), to right. Animations 3 and 14.
Sprites $94-$98: the fuzzy with a bow walking left (animation 4): Clyde's friend in the last scene.
Sprites $99-$9D: the fuzzy with a bow walking right (animation 5): some of the posse, and Clyde's friend.
Sprite $9E: Clyde standing facing left, as he waits by his shack in the second scene (animation 6).
Sprites $9F-$A3 and on to $A4: facing left, he reaches an arm out and draws it back, beckoning (animation 7).
Sprites $A4-$A8: turning from facing left ($A4) through facing out ($A6) to facing right ($A8). Animations 8 (backwards), 11, 12 and 13 play them.
Sprites $A9 and $AA: a big and a small heart, single colour; animation 9 alternates them, so the hearts beat.

Sprite $AB: three wide stripes. Sprite 0 shows it in orange behind the shack's wall in the second and third scenes. Sprites with lower numbers are drawn over higher ones, so it covers the fuzzies (sprites 1-7) where the wall has gaps between its logs, and they seem to go in through the wall (checked live: with sprite 0 off, they show through the gaps).

The first scene's screen, 1000 characters copied to $4400 by draw_village, then 24 zero bytes to $6EFF. Rows 0-2 are empty sky (character $FF); the stump houses of the village and its trees stand on rows 3-13, and rows 14-24 are the cliff of grey rocks.

The second and third scenes' screen, 1000 characters copied to $4400 by draw_shack: Clyde's log shack at night under a crescent moon and stars, on a strip of ground. It uses characters $12-$7A and the blank $FF.
24 bytes after shack_screen that nothing reads: a fragment of 6502 code (LDA $7CDB,Y / STA $7CDA ...), left over when the file was saved.

The colour of each character of village_chars, 256 bytes: colour_screen sets each cell's colour RAM from this table, indexed by the character code. The values used are 0 (single-colour black) and 8, 9, 11, 13, 14 and 15: multicolour characters (bit 3) whose own colour is black, white, cyan, green, blue or yellow.

The colour of each character of shack_chars, the same way, for the second and third scenes. Only the entries for characters $12-$7A and $FF are read (the last falls in f_74FB), so the tables below start in its unused tail at $747B.

The ending's 16 sprite animations, set by anim_set from four tables of 16: this one the kind of each (0 a still frame, 1 a loop, 2 back and forth, 3 forward once and hold the last frame, 4 backwards once). By number: 0 walk left ($84-$88), 1 walk right ($89-$8D), 2 facing out ($8E), 3 the bowed fuzzy turns from left to right ($8F-$93), 4 and 5 the bowed fuzzy walks left ($94-$98) and right ($99-$9D), 6 Clyde waiting ($9E), 7 beckoning ($9F-$A4), 8 turning from right to left ($A7 down to $A4), 9 the beating heart ($A9/$AA), 10 the stripes ($AB), 11 and 12 turning from left to right ($A4-$A8; 12 at half speed), 13 turning from left to facing out ($A4-$A6), 14 the bowed fuzzy turning from left to facing out ($8F-$91), 15 the sparkle ($81, $82, then the empty $83).
Each animation's first sprite.
Each animation's frame count: for kind 1 the frames shown, for kinds 2 and 3 the frames after the first, for kind 4 the frames played backwards from first + count - 1.
Each animation's frames per step: how many frames each picture stays on.

The first scene's sprite x positions, low bytes (all eight have their $D010 bit set, so they start at x $1C8, $1FF, $1ED, $1FF, $1FF, $156, $1BC and $16D, off the screen, and come in at the left as their x goes round from $1FF to 0).

The second scene's sprite x positions: sprite 0 (the stripes) at $96, sprites 1-6 at $1ED, $1CF, $1A7, $191, $178 and $156 (high bits $7E: off the screen, to come in at the left), Clyde (sprite 7) at $64.
The first scene's frames per step for each sprite, over the animation's own: 4, 5, 5, 5, 4, 4, 4, 4.
The frame each sprite's animation starts on, in the first and third scenes (0, 0, 2, 0, 3, 2, 1, 0), so that the walkers are out of step.
The pixels each sprite moves at a step to the right (sprite_right): the first scene's 1, 1, 1, 1, 2, 2, 2, 2. The second and third scenes copy f_74E3 over it.
The second and third scenes' steps to the right: 0, 1, 2, 2, 2, 2, 1, 1.
The animation each sprite starts with in the first scene: 1 (walk right) for Clyde and sprites 2 and 4-7, 5 (the bowed fuzzy walking right) for sprites 1 and 3.
The second scene's animations: 10 (the stripes) for sprite 0, 1 for sprites 1 and 3-5, 5 for sprites 2 and 6, 6 (waiting) for Clyde, sprite 7.

The third scene's animations: 10 for sprite 0, 0 (walk left) for sprites 1, 3, 4, 5 and Clyde, 4 (the bowed fuzzy walking left) for sprite 2 and his friend, sprite 6. Its fifth byte, 0, is also the colour shack_colours gives the blank character $FF.
One bit for each sprite, $01 to $80: the bit to flip in $D010 or set in $D015.
How many frames each of the gang (sprites 1-5) waits before leaving in the third scene: 48, 72, 97, 115 and 143. The first byte, for sprite 0, is not read.
The x of the five hearts (sprites 1-5): $6F, $6C, $6D, $6F and $7A, between Clyde and his friend.
How many steps of hearts_rise (one every other frame) each heart waits before it appears: 16, 32, 48, 64 and 80, read from the second byte; the first is f_7513's last.

To $77FF, 739 bytes that nothing in the ending reads: 6502 code (JSR $75D0 at $7538, RTS at $7558, and more) and tables at $772E-$77FF, left over when the file was saved. They match no other file on the disks.

The character set of the second and third scenes, at $D018 = $1E (characters $7800, screen $4400). Only characters $12-$7A, to $7BD7, are drawn, and $FF, the blank at $7FF8. Characters 0-$11 hold shapes the screen does not use, and $7B-$FE fall on the ending's text, code and leftovers. A zero byte at $7BD8 comes before the first string.
"GAME COMPLETE" and $FF: print_big's string 5 while the ending is in, printed in big letters at the top.

"HAVING EXTERMINATED THE EARTH RIDDEN SLIME AND SAVED HIS CUTE AND CUDDLY LITTLE FRIENDS, CLYDE LEADS THE POSSE BACK TO THE VILLAGE." and $FF (print_at's string 4), padded with spaces so each line breaks at a word: the first scene.
"IN TRADITIONAL FUZZY FASHION CLYDE INVITES THE GANG TO A RAVE AT HIS SHACK THAT NIGHT." and $FF (string 5): the second scene.
"FOLLOWING THE CELEBRATIONS, CLYDE AND HIS LADY FRIEND MAKE UP FOR LOST TIME." and $FF (string 6): the third scene.
"THE END" and $FF: print_big's string 6.
"WHY NOT USE THE CHEAT MODE NEXT TIME" and $FF (print_at's string 7), printed only when the game was finished without the cheat.
The low bytes of big strings 5 and 6 ($7BD9, $7D25), copied into print_big_lo.
The low bytes of print_at's strings 4-7 ($7BE7, $7C74, $7CD6, $7D2D), copied into print_at_lo.
The high bytes of big strings 5 and 6, copied into print_big_hi.
The high bytes of print_at's strings 4-7, copied into print_at_hi.
The text screen's colour counter: counts passes of its wait loop down from 20.
The text screen's place in f_7D60, counting down from 7 to 0 and round again.
The eight colours the letters take in turn, read from the end: black, dark grey, green, light green, yellow, light red, purple, blue. Then two bytes nothing reads (0F 00).

The ending, entered from the engine's loader_hand_over ($BE47) once stage 10's file has loaded to $5800-$8CFF. Interrupts off, BASIC banked out with the KERNAL and I/O in ($01 = $36), VIC bank 1, black border and background, sprites off, the screen cleared to character $FF in black (clear_screen). The text character set comes in from $D000 (memory_swap 6, the same swap the Get Ready screen uses) and is inverted (charset_invert).
Points print_big's strings 5 and 6 and print_at's strings 4-7 at the ending's own text (f_7D52-f_7D5A), in the engine's tables at $34A8, $34BB, $33BD and $33D3.
Rewrites frame_music ($8009) as JSR $0873 (music_frame) and RTS, for the scenes' raster routines.
Prints "GAME COMPLETE" in big letters at $4407 (row 0) and "THE END" at $46B5 (row 17), and the three paragraphs of the story at rows 4, 9 and 13.
The story's three paragraphs (print_at strings 4, 5 and 6) at $44A2, $456B and $460A.
Unless the cheat is on (three NOPs at $1CA0, written by the attract's title_cheat_step), prints "WHY NOT USE THE CHEAT MODE NEXT TIME" at row 22.

Screen on, then the colour cycle until fire. The inverted set leaves each letter's own pixels clear, so they show the background colour $D021 and the rest of each character is the black of colour RAM: changing $D021 changes the letters' colour. The loop waits for the raster's low byte to be 0 and counts a_7D5E down on each pass; a pass is quicker than a raster line, so with interrupts off the colour changes every two or three frames (measured), cycling eight colours about two and a half times a second.
Fire on joystick 2 ($DC00 bit 4) leaves the loop.

Clears the screen, inverts the text set back and swaps it out to $D000 again (memory_swap 6), starts the ending tune (music_play, ending_tune at $88C5) with all three voices and the volume at 15, and runs the three scenes (end_scenes).

After the scenes: music_frame now copies only registers $17 down to 0 ($087C = $17), leaving the volume register $D418 to this loop, which turns it down a step at a time from 15 while the last scene stays on the screen. The count a_7E6A is passes of a wait for raster line 0, about four a frame, so the first step comes about 32 frames on and each next one about 24: some eight seconds to silence (measured).
The volume being faded, from 15 down.
The fade's pass counter: 200 before the first step, then 100.

Clears the screen, turns the sprites off and goes back to the beginning: stage $FF, so stage_next makes it stage 0 and reloads the attract block and level 1.1, with end_flag 1 (X), which loader_hand_over takes as it does after the last life: into the attract block at $E503 and the high-score check.
Both screens to character $FF and colour RAM to black (screen_fill).
To $7FFF, sprite shapes (blocks $FA-$FF, from $7E80) that the ending never shows: 377 of these 381 bytes are the same as level 1.1's file here, left over when the file was saved.
Nine bytes of code with no entry (LDA $DD00 / AND #$FC / ORA #$02 / STA ...), the same instructions scene_village starts with, cut off by frame_music at $8009.

Called once a frame by the scenes' raster routines ($81FB, $823F). In the file it is DEC $D020, a delay loop of 150 passes and INC $D020, which would draw a band of another colour in the border; ending_start rewrites it as JSR music_frame and RTS before the scenes start.
Operand of the DEC at $8009, which ending_start rewrites as $73: the low byte of music_frame.
High byte of the DEC's operand, rewritten as $08.
LDY #$00 in the file, rewritten as $60, RTS: the delay loop after it is never reached once the ending runs.
A second RTS after frame_music's own, which nothing reaches.
The three scenes in turn: the walk back to the village, the rave at Clyde's shack and the pair.

The first scene. VIC bank 1 ($DD00), screen $4400 with village_chars ($D018 = $16), multicolour text, black border; frame flag $4801, step $4802 and step delay $4804 cleared. With the screen off it places the sprites (sprites_village) and draws the scene (draw_village), turns the screen on at line $FF and starts the raster routines at line $64 (raster_start). Then once a frame (the flag $4801 set by the routine at line $FF): the sprite animations (anim_all) and the scene's script (village_script), until the script reaches step 11.
With the screen off: the sprites, the picture and its colours; screen on at line $FF, then the raster routines from raster_village_rocks at line $64.
Middle byte of the JSR at $8050. The label is the engine's: loader_hand_over jumps to $8051, where a torture chamber's file starts; in the ending it falls inside this instruction.
The frame loop: waits for the flag the routine at line $FF sets, steps the animations and the script, clears the flag; until step 11.
The second scene: set up by rave_setup, then once a frame the animations, rave_script and rave_group, until step 8.
The third scene, on the same screen and raster routines: pair_setup, then once a frame the animations, pair_script and pair_group, until step 7.
village_screen to the screen and its colours from village_colours.
shack_screen to the screen and its colours from shack_colours.
Copies 25 rows of 40 characters from the address in $02/$03 to the screen at $4400.
Next row: both pointers on by 40, 25 rows in all.
Sets the colour RAM from the screen: each cell takes the byte of the table at $02/$03 (a page) indexed by its character. $4800 holds Y while the character is the index.
Each cell: the character from the screen ($06/$07) is the index, Y kept at $4800 meanwhile, and the table's byte goes to colour RAM ($04/$05).
Next row: the screen and colour RAM pointers on by 40, 25 rows.

Starts the scenes' raster interrupt at line A with the routine at X (low) and Y (high): points the vectors at $FFFE and $0314 at raster_irq (the first is in the RAM under the KERNAL, unused with $01 = $36), turns off the CIA interrupts, clears any pending, enables the raster interrupt, sets $D011 to $1B and stops CIA 1's timer A.
CIA 1 and 2 interrupts off ($7F to $DC0D and $DD0D) and any pending cleared by reading them.
The raster interrupt on, any pending acknowledged, $D011 = $1B, and CIA 1's timer A stopped; interrupts back on.
The same for the second scene, with the vectors already set: line A, routine X/Y.

The raster interrupt. It saves A, X and Y in the immediates at raster_exit, acknowledges the interrupt and calls the current routine, which returns the next routine's line in A and its address in X and Y; those go to $D012 and the JSR. Then three PLAs drop the copies of Y, X and A the KERNAL's handler pushed (the interrupt arrives through it, $01 being $36, and $0314), and raster_exit restores the registers and returns.
Operand of the JSR at $81BB, low byte: the raster routine to run, written by raster_start and by each run.
High byte of the JSR's operand.
LDA, LDX and LDY of the registers raster_irq saved in their operands, then RTI.
Operand of the LDA at $81CA: A as the interrupt found it.
Operand of the LDX: X as the interrupt found it.
Operand of the LDY: Y as the interrupt found it.
First scene, at line $A8 (line $64 the first time): the cliff's colours, background light grey, multicolours dark grey and mid grey. Next: raster_village_sky at line $FF.

First scene, at line $FF: sets the frame flag $4801, the sky and village colours for the top of the next frame (background light blue, multicolours brown and orange) and plays the music (frame_music). Next: raster_village_rocks at line $A8.
Second and third scenes, at line $9B (line $64 the first time): multicolours orange and brown for the shack's log walls. Next: raster_shack_ground at line $C9.
At line $C9: after nine NOPs, a short delay, multicolours light blue and dark grey for the ground. Next: raster_shack_roof at line $FF.
At line $FF: the frame flag $4801, multicolours light red and brown for the roof at the top of the next frame, and the music. Next: raster_shack_walls at line $9B.

Steps each sprite's animation, 0-7. Per sprite at $4806+X: the kind ($4806, 0 for none), first frame ($480E), count ($4816), frames per step ($481E), position ($4826), frame counter ($482E) and direction ($4836). When the counter runs out it is reloaded, and kind 1 steps by anim_loop, kinds 2 and 3 by anim_swing and kind 4 by anim_backward; each writes the frame to the sprite's pointer at $47F8+X.
This sprite's counter has run out: reloaded from its frames per step, then the step for its kind.
Kind 1: the position goes round 0 to count-1; the frame is first + position.

Kinds 2 and 3: the position moves by the direction, which turns to +1 at 0 and to -1 at the count, so the frame swings between first and first + count. Kind 3 stops (kind 0) on reaching first + count.
At the count: kind 3 becomes 0 (stopped), and the direction turns to -1.
The frame: first + position, to the sprite's pointer.
Kind 4: the position counts up and the frame is first + count - position, from first + count - 1 down to first, where it stops (kind 0).

The first scene's sprites: all eight light red multicolour (dark grey and yellow), x from f_74BB with the high bits set, y $92, in front of the scenery and unexpanded. Each starts its animation from f_74EB (anim_set), on the frame from f_74D3, with its frames per step from f_74CB.
Each sprite's animation from f_74EB, its starting frame from f_74D3 and frames per step from f_74CB; sprite 5's frames per step set to 4 again after.
$4823, sprite 5's frames per step, set to 4, which f_74CB already gave it.
All eight multicolour and on, all with their $D010 bits set; no expansion, all in front of the scenery; multicolours dark grey and yellow.
The second scene's sprites: x from f_74C3, y $B5, steps to the right from f_74E3, animations from f_74F3, all behind the scenery; sprite 0, the stripes, in orange.
Each sprite's animation from f_74F3.
All multicolour, on and behind the scenery; $D010 = $7E for sprites 1-6; no expansion; multicolours dark grey and yellow; sprite 0 orange.
The third scene's sprites: all eight at x $98, y $B5, inside the shack behind the wall and the stripes; steps from f_74E3, animations from f_74FB, starting frames from f_74D3; sprite 0 orange.
Each sprite's animation from f_74FB and starting frame from f_74D3.
All $D010 bits clear; sprite 0 orange.
Starts animation Y on sprite X: its kind, first frame (also the sprite's pointer now), count and frames per step from the tables at f_747B, position 0, direction +1.
Frames per step into both the setting and the counter; position 0, direction +1.
Moves sprite X right by its step from f_74DB, flipping its bit of $D010 when x passes 255.
Moves sprite X one pixel left, flipping its bit of $D010 when x passes 0.
The first scene's script: while the step delay $4804 runs, nothing; then each of the routines below, each acting only at its own step of $4802. Clyde is sprite 0.
The ten steps' routines, last step first, so that a step taken by one routine is not acted on by the next in the same frame.
Step 0: Clyde walks in from the left until x $B0, then turns to face left (animation 8, first frame $A8) and the script waits 80 frames.
At x $B0: step 1, animation 8 with kind 4 and the pointer at $A8 (facing right) to start from, and 80 frames.
Not there yet: Clyde moves right by his step.
Step 1: once he has turned, he beckons (animation 7); 42 frames.
Steps 2 and 3: when the last beckon has ended, another; 42 frames each. Three beckons in all.
Step 4: he turns to face right (animation 11).
Step 5: once his turn to the right has ended, Clyde walks on (animation 1).
Step 6: Clyde walks right until x $105, past the middle of the screen.
Step 7: Clyde and sprites 1 and 2 walk on until Clyde is at x $178, off the right edge.
Step 8: sprites 1-7, the posse, walk across (4-7 at two pixels a step) until sprite 2 is at x $160, off the screen.
Step 9: sprite 3, the last of the posse, crosses alone until x $155; then 50 frames.
Step 10: step 11, which ends the scene.

The second scene: $D018 = $1E (shack_chars), black background, steps cleared, the script waiting 50 frames; with the screen off, sprites_rave and draw_shack; then the screen on and the raster routines from raster_shack_walls at line $64 (raster_restart).
With the screen off: sprites_rave, draw_shack; screen on, then the raster routines from raster_shack_walls at line $64.
The third scene: the same screen settings, steps cleared and the script waiting 250 frames (the party inside).
The second scene's script; Clyde is sprite 7, waiting by his shack. While $4804 runs, nothing; then the routines below at their steps.
Each frame (unless $4805 holds it back), rave_walk_in.

Steps 0 and 1: when his last animation has ended, Clyde beckons (animation 7), 42 frames. The first sets the posse walking (group step $4803 = 1) after 50 frames; after the second the script waits 170.
The test of Clyde's animation kind ($480D), 0 when it has ended. The label is the engine's: it reads a level's map data here.
After the first beckon (step 1): the posse starts in 50 frames ($4805). After the second (step 2): the script waits 170 frames.
Steps 2 and 3: two more beckons, 42 frames each: four in all.
Step 4: he turns to face right, slowly (animation 12).
Step 5: once his turn to the right has ended, Clyde walks (animation 1) towards the shack.
Step 6: Clyde walks right until x $95, behind the stripes: into his shack; then 50 frames.
Step 7: step 8, which ends the scene.

With group step 1: sprites 1-6 walk right, in from the left, each until it reaches x $95 and stands behind the stripes, inside. It then checks whether sprites 0-6 are all at $8C or more, but returns the same way whatever it finds.
The check of sprites 0-6 against x $8C, whose result nothing uses.
The third scene's script; Clyde is sprite 7 and his friend sprite 6. While $4804 runs, nothing; then the routines below at their steps.
Unless $4805 holds it back, the gang (gang_leave) and the hearts (hearts_rise).
Operand of the DEC at $8708 ($4805). The label is the engine's: a level's map row pointers start at $8709.
High byte of the DEC's operand. The label is the engine's.

Step 0: Clyde walks out of the shack to the left, and his friend follows once he is past x $84, until she is at x $78. Then the gang starts leaving (group step 1), Clyde turns to face out (animation 13) and she does too (animation 14); 24 frames.
High byte of the LDA's operand ($4802). The label is the engine's.
Step 1: when sprite 5, the last of the gang, is left of x $50, she turns back to face left, towards Clyde: her pointer steps down to $8F every eight frames.
There: her pointer steps down to $8F, one frame every eight; at $8F, step 2.
Step 2: Clyde turns to face right, towards her: his pointer steps up to $A8 every eight frames; then the script waits 140 frames, while the hearts rise.
Step 3: she turns from left to right (animation 3); 42 frames.
Step 4: both walk right (animations 5 and 1), changing frame every six frames.
Step 5, every other frame: each walks right until x $96, behind the stripes. When Clyde is in, 50 frames.
High byte of the LDA's operand ($D00C, sprite 6's x). The label is the engine's.
Step 6: step 7, which ends the scene.

With group step 1: each of sprites 1-5 waits its time from f_750B, then walks left a pixel a frame. When all five have passed the left edge (their $D010 bits set, $3E), group step 2: sprites 1-5 become the hearts: single colour, red, animation 9, at the x of f_7513 and y $AF, and hidden ($D015 = $C1) until each one's turn.
All five off the left edge ($D010 = $3E): group step 2 and the hearts set up.
The hearts' positions from f_7513, y $AF; $D010 cleared.
With group step 2, every other frame: each heart appears when its wait in f_7517 runs out, and rises a pixel until y $63. Once above y $96 a heart bursts into the sparkle (animation 15) and vanishes.
Each heart that is out rises a pixel until y $63.
Above y $96 and still showing a heart (pointer $A8 or more): the sparkle, animation 15; $4800 keeps Y meanwhile.
High byte of the STY's operand ($4800). The label is the engine's.
Blanks the screen ($D011 bit 4 off).
Waits for raster line $FF and turns the screen back on.
One byte between the code and the tune that nothing reads ($20).

The ending's tune, in the music driver's format: a header of two voice offsets ($007D and $013C from the first voice), then the three voices from $88C9, $8946 and $8A05, each ending in the end command ($1E), and the sections the third voice calls from $8BD2 to $8C35.
ending_tune's second voice, to $8A04.
Part of ending_tune's second voice, 15 bytes in. The label is the engine's, which reads a level's tables here ($3B81).
ending_tune's third voice, to its end at $8BD1, much of it calls ($23) of the sections that follow.
Part of ending_tune's third voice, 16 bytes in. The label is the engine's ($3B8D).
Part of ending_tune's third voice, 208 bytes in. The label is the engine's ($3B99).
Part of ending_tune's third voice, 400 bytes in. The label is the engine's: a level's length in scroll positions.
The next byte of the third voice. The label is the engine's: a level's first character that Clyde can pass through.
Part of ending_tune's third voice, 402 bytes in. The label is the engine's: a level's multicolour 1 table.
Part of ending_tune's third voice, near its end. The label is the engine's: a level's multicolour 2 table.
The sections ending_tune's third voice calls, $8BD2, $8BFA, $8C05, $8C14 and $8C29, each ending in a return ($24).
Part of ending_tune's first section. The label is the engine's.
A section in the music format, ending in a return ($24) at $8BF9, that ending_tune never calls.
Part of ending_tune's second section. The label is the engine's.
Part of ending_tune's fourth section. The label is the engine's.
ending_tune's last section, to its return at $8C35. The label is the engine's.
Part of ending_tune's last section. The label is the engine's.
The last section's return ($24). The label is the engine's.
Another section in the music format, to a return at $8C4C, that ending_tune never calls.
Part of tune_unused_2, 5 bytes in. The label is the engine's.
